claim: WAVTBL row format: byte0 HIGH nibble is WBOUND, the number of bounders in the wave (JOUSTRV4.SRC:175).

source.verbatim: WBOUND	RMB	0	NBR OF BOUNDERS IN THIS WAVE (UPPER NIBBLE)

claim: WAVTBL row format: byte0 LOW nibble is WHUNT, the number of hunters in the wave (JOUSTRV4.SRC:176).

source.verbatim: WHUNT	RMB	1	NBR OF HUNTERS IN THIS WAVE (LOWER NIBBLE)

claim: WAVTBL row format: byte1 LOW nibble is WPERSUE, the pursuit nibble that seeds WSMART (JOUSTRV4.SRC:178).

source.verbatim: WPERSUE	RMB	1	NBR OF PERSUERS IN THIS WAVE (LOWER NIBBLE)

claim: WAVTBL row format: byte3 is WSTATUS, the whole status byte (cliff bits | JSR type bits | persue bit) (JOUSTRV4.SRC:180).

source.verbatim: WSTATUS	RMB	1	STATUS BYTE FOR THIS WAVE

claim: Status bit WBPER = $01, the instantaneous-pursue flag — below the JSR type mask, so it never leaks into the wave type (JOUSTRV4.SRC:185).

source.verbatim: WBPER	EQU	$01	IF=1, PERSUE WILL BE INSTANTANIOUSLY

claim: Status bit WBJSR0 = $02, the low bit of the 3-bit JSR-table offset that selects the wave type (JOUSTRV4.SRC:186).

source.verbatim: WBJSR0	EQU	$02	THESE 3 BITS ARE A JSR TABLE OFFSET

claim: Status bit WBJSR1 = $04; the comment lists the JSR offsets 0,2,4,6,8,10,12,14, but WJSRTB implements only six — offsets 12 and 14 are phantom, in no wave (JOUSTRV4.SRC:187).

source.verbatim: WBJSR1	EQU	$04	 (0 = AN NOP, OTHERS ARE 2,4,6,8,10,12,14)

claim: Status bit WBCL1L = $10 records CLIFF1L destroyed — a high-nibble cliff-destruction DATA bit, no behaviour in jt2-5 (JOUSTRV4.SRC:189).

source.verbatim: WBCL1L	EQU	$10	IF=1, CLIFF1L IS DISABLED (OR DESTROYED)

claim: Composite cliff mask WBCL1 = WBCL1L+WBCL1R = $30 — derived from its primitives, not hand-typed (JOUSTRV4.SRC:193).
Composite cliff mask WBCLS = WBCL1+WBCL2+WBCL4 = $F0, all cliffs — the high-nibble data mask (JOUSTRV4.SRC:197).
The wave number is an independent BCD counter: LDA WAVBCD reads the BCD wave number (0-99), distinct from the WAVTBL pointer (JOUSTRV4.SRC:2001).
DAA decimal-adjusts the incremented wave number, making it BCD: 0x09+1 = 0x10 (not 0x0A), 0x99+1 = 0x00 (JOUSTRV4.SRC:2003).
PWAVE is seeded to WAVTBL-WLEN — one row BEFORE wave 1 — then advanced before the first wave, so wave 0 is never played (JOUSTRV4.SRC:1878).
Loop-at-81: after advancing one WLEN row per wave, CMPX #WTBEND tests for the end of the table (JOUSTRV4.SRC:2018).
Loop-at-81: at end of table the pointer restarts at WTBRST (wave 81), so the late-wave plateau repeats forever (JOUSTRV4.SRC:2020).

source.verbatim: LDX	#WTBRST		YES, RESTART AT NEW POINT

claim: WAVTBL wave 1 row = $30,$01,0,2 — 3 bounders, 1 pursuer, status 2 (the intro wave) (JOUSTRV4.SRC:2439).
WTBRST wave 81 row = $00,$AF,0,... — no bounders/hunters, all shadow lords ($A) at max pursuit ($F): the $00,$AF plateau (JOUSTRV4.SRC:2535).
WTBEND closes the wave table — END OF WAVE TABLE, REPEAT AT WTBRST (the loop-back point) (JOUSTRV4.SRC:2546).

source.verbatim: WTBEND	EQU	*			END OF WAVE TABLE, REPEAT AT "WTBRST"

claim: WJSRTB dispatch masks the status low nibble to the JSR bits: ANDB #WBJSR0+WBJSR1+WBJSR2 = & $0E (JOUSTRV4.SRC:2042).
WJSRTB dispatch calls the wave-type routine indirectly through the six-entry table: JSR [B,X] (JOUSTRV4.SRC:2044).
WJSRTB[0] = WAVRTS, the NOP wave type (index 0) (JOUSTRV4.SRC:2586).
WJSRTB[5] = WPTERO, the pterodactyl wave type (index 5, JSR offset 10) — the last of the six real types (JOUSTRV4.SRC:2591).
Degrade law: a WCOOP co-op wave checks player 2 alive (SPLY2+6) — two players only (JOUSTRV4.SRC:2628).

source.verbatim: WCOOP	LDA	SPLY2+6		THIS MESSAGE IS FOR TWO PLAYERS ONLY

claim: Degrade law: when a player is out, a co-op wave degrades to survival — BEQ WAVSUR (JOUSTRV4.SRC:2629).

source.verbatim: BEQ	WAVSUR		 BR=PLAYER 2 DEAD, GO TO SURVIVAL WAVE

claim: Degrade law: a WGLAD gladiator wave checks player 1 alive (SPLY1+6) — two players only (JOUSTRV4.SRC:2697).

source.verbatim: WGLAD	LDA	SPLY1+6		THIS MESSAGE IS FOR TWO PLAYERS ONLY

claim: Degrade law: a gladiator wave no-ops (BEQ WAVRT2 → RTS) when a player is out — solo it does nothing (JOUSTRV4.SRC:2698).
Message beat timing is ~1 s and unpinned: LDA #180/6 is a message-loop count, WAIT A SECOND — the shell owns timing (JOUSTRV4.SRC:2045).
The intro reset ~1 s delay is LDA #90/6, a 1 SECOND DELAY — approximate, not an exact-frame beat duration (JOUSTRV4.SRC:2601).
IFN DEBUG death oracle: the death path fires only for an enemy — LDA PID,U reads the DEAD ENEMY process id (JOUSTRV4.SRC:2954).

source.verbatim: LDA	PID,U	THIS IS A DEAD ENEMY ISN'T IT?

claim: IFN DEBUG death oracle: CMPA #EMYID confirms it is an enemy before decrementing NENEMY (JOUSTRV4.SRC:2955).
IFN DEBUG oracle: after DEC NENEMY the count must not go negative — BPL 45$ else the author SWIs (JOUSTRV4.SRC:2967).
